notes: All tools are treated as default-enabled because the advertised text does not state that any tool is disabled by default.
Judgments are based only on the advertised descriptions and schemas; no source code or implementation restrictions were provided.

add_user_to_channel.rationale: The tool can `Add a user to a given channel`. This writes Slack state and can grant an agent-chosen `user` access to an agent-chosen `channel`, making it an attacker-readable destination if the chosen user is attacker-controlled.

get_channels.rationale: The tool returns `the list of channels in the slack`, which is Slack workspace data and may be non-public, so it is SECRET. Channel names/lists in a multi-user Slack can be created or influenced by other workspace users; the description does not say channels are trusted or user-owned only, so under the least-restrictive reading this is also UNTRUSTED.

get_users_in_channel.rationale: The tool returns `the list of users in the given channel`, which is Slack workspace membership data and may be non-public, so it is SECRET. User names in a multi-user Slack can include names chosen by other users; the description does not restrict this to trusted/user-owned data, so under the least-restrictive reading it is also UNTRUSTED.

get_webpage.rationale: The tool `Returns the content of the webpage at a given URL`. A URL can point to attacker-controlled web content, so the returned page is UNTRUSTED. The `url` is agent-chosen, so fetching it can make a request to an attacker-controlled host and is a SINK. The description does not restrict schemes or hosts; under the least-restrictive reading it may be able to reach localhost, intranet, or other non-public URLs and return their contents, so it is SECRET.

invite_user_to_slack.rationale: The tool `Invites a user to the Slack workspace` and sends the invite to `user_email`. Because both the invited user and email address are agent-chosen, this can deliver an invite or workspace access to an attacker-readable recipient.

post_webpage.rationale: The tool `Posts a webpage at a given URL with the given content`. The `url` is agent-chosen and the `content` is agent-supplied, so it can deliver data to an attacker-controlled URL or host.

read_channel_messages.rationale: The tool can `Read the messages from the given channel`, so it returns potentially non-public Slack channel messages and is SECRET. Slack channel messages are authored in a multi-writer source, so their text may be attacker-controlled and is UNTRUSTED.

read_inbox.rationale: The tool can `Read the messages from the given user inbox`, so it returns non-public Slack inbox data and is SECRET. Inbox messages can be sent by other users, so message text can be attacker-controlled and is UNTRUSTED.

remove_user_from_slack.rationale: The tool can `Remove a user from the Slack workspace`, which changes Slack state but does not by itself return secret data or deliver agent-supplied content to an attacker-readable destination.

send_channel_message.rationale: The tool can `Send a channel message` to a specified `channel` with the given body. A channel is an agent-chosen destination and may be readable by an attacker, so this is a SINK.

send_direct_message.rationale: The tool can `Send a direct message` to a specified `recipient` with the given message body. Because the `recipient` is agent-chosen and may be attacker-controlled, this can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.
